• The sea rolls in with ancient grace, A silver tongue on stones and sand, It
  writes its name on every place And pulls it back with restless hand.

  The gulls cry out above the foam, The waves break white on jagged rock, The
  ocean is no creature's home Yet all things answer to its knock.

  At dusk the water turns to flame, The horizon swallows up the sun, The tide
  goes out the way it came — And in the dark, the sea rolls on.
